A drug-trafficking operation was registered on Wednesday 4 November in Água
Clara. Military Police received information that a man was selling drugs
from a white VW Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. When
officers found the car, the driver tried to flee and was caught and stopped
after a chase lasting a few blocks. In the car officers found a portion of
a substance resembling cocaine, and at the suspect's home they seized portions
of marijuana, a precision scale, drug-packaging materials and money.

A task force of the Military Police and Civil Police then found two other people
involved at a snack bar. Information gathered during the incident led teams
to a drug hideout in a wooded area near the MS-324 highway. The teams
seized 59 tablets of a substance resembling marijuana, weighing about 54
kilograms.

The three people involved were taken to the Água Clara Civil Police station for
legal proceedings.

specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside

mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remained open amid suspicion of larger cargo shipments and heavy vehicles being concealed in spaces used as storehouses, or 'zulos', for hashish.

transported the drugs, finding two kilograms of cocaine, several doses, cutting
agent, a 9mm pistol with cartridges, a bow and arrows and a hydraulic press for
compressing cocaine. A further person was arrested for involvement in the

sale and said the investigation remained open, with further arrests not ruled
out. Officers from the Unidad de Prevención y Reacción, the Grupo II de

three-story detached house in a housing estate. The seized cannabis buds

In Mustafakemalpaşa district of Bursa province, the 2010 shotgun murder of
Mehmet Arıcan was solved 16 years later. The murder was determined to have
been committed over a dispute caused by unauthorized entry into a cannabis
field; of 17 suspects detained, one was remanded in custody.

neighbourhood, Mustafakemalpaşa. Arıcan worked as a construction worker and
disappeared after leaving his workplace, with no further word from him. His
body was found four days later at Karanlıkdere, and examination showed he had
been shot and killed with a shotgun in the forest.

Three suspects detained after the killing were freed when prosecutors decided
there were no grounds for prosecution, and the file was moved to permanent
search. Sixteen years later, under the Mustafakemalpaşa Chief Public
Prosecutor's Office, investigators re-examined phone records, financial
inquiries and new witness statements and carried out field work in Taşpınar.

Jasat teams staged simultaneous operations at eight addresses on 11 November and
caught 17 suspects. Of the detainees, H.F. was remanded by the court after
being taken to it, while 16 suspects were released. At the time of the
killing, Arıcan and H.F. were in dispute over unauthorized entry into a cannabis

notified of suspicion under Articles 307 and 310 of the Criminal Code.

prosecutor's office said he partly admitted guilt but that the evidence
established both offences in full. The verdict has not entered legal force. Korabelov.info reported that, according to police, the collected evidence

report.body:
Rogelio Lorenzo Francisca, 32, from Guerrero, Mexico, was arrested during a
search warrant in Taft, California, and booked into the Taft jail facility.
He was arrested on suspicion of cultivation of marijuana, marijuana for sales,
conspiracy and delay/resist/obstruct arrest, according to the Kern County
Sheriff's Office.

Deputies eradicated a total of 660 marijuana plants during the search.
Dangerous pesticides were also found within the grow site. Another account
described the same operation as yielding 660 marijuana plants and dangerous
pesticides at the cultivation site.

The warrant was executed on October 8, 2026, in the 27000 block of Highway 119
in Taft by deputies assigned to the Taft substation, assisted by the Sheriff's
Office High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas Task Force (KC-HIDTA) and the Taft
Police Department. The location was also described as the 27000 block of
Taft Highway. The Sheriff's Office said the investigation was active and
ongoing. The Sheriff's Office asked anyone with information to contact it
or Kern Secret Witness.

attempts.decision_title: Legalisation law change belongs in the CFI
attempts.explanation: The submitted Al Jazeera feature reports that President Cyril Ramaphosa signed the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act on 26 May 2024, one day before the general election, making private cultivation and use lawful in South Africa. Its substance is a change in the law and a policy explainer, framed with historical background on prohibition, court rulings, a 2023 police order to stop pot busts, and the Eswatini hemp-growing debate. It is not a single enforcement event with figures. Under the tracker's scope rules, law changes, precedents and national-level policy belong in the Cannabis Freedom Index history, not the enforcement tracker. The passing reference to a 2020 raid on the Haze Club carries no date detail, figures or outcome and does not establish a separate reportable event.

attempts.decision_title: Law change belongs in CFI history
attempts.explanation: The submitted Al Jazeera feature reports that President Cyril Ramaphosa signed the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act on 26 May 2024, legalising private cultivation and use of cannabis in South Africa and automatically expunging related records. This is a change to the law, and the tracker's scope covers only individual enforcement events such as raids, seizures, arrests, prosecutions and sentences. The article's references to raids, arrests, herbicide spraying and the roughly 3,000 people imprisoned for cannabis offences are historical background or national statistics, not the event the page reports and not a single enforcement action that could form a tracker report. Law changes, legalisation and national statistics belong to the Cannabis Freedom Index history, so no tracker report is drafted here.
